Describe TWO OR THREE specific lines of evidence that support the endosymbiotic origin of mitochondria.

Part B: Describe the role of the inner mitochondrial membrane in ATP synthesis. In your answer, explain: (i) the source of the proton gradient; (ii) how the proton gradient drives ATP synthesis through ATP synthase; and (iii) the general role of the electron transport chain complexes (supplied in the stimulus) in building that gradient.

Part C: A researcher adds the following compounds to isolated mitochondria respiring aerobically. For each compound, predict whether O₂ consumption and ATP synthesis will increase, decrease, or be unaffected, and explain your reasoning:
Rotenone (inhibits Complex I electron transfer)
Oligomycin (blocks the F₀ channel of ATP synthase)
Dinitrophenol / DNP (uncoupler — makes the inner membrane permeable to H⁺)

Part D: Heart muscle cells have unusually high numbers of mitochondria. Explain the functional reason for this, and describe the specific structural feature of mitochondria that maximizes ATP output.
stimulus:
Mitochondrial structure:
• Outer membrane: permeable to small molecules (porins)
• Intermembrane space: H⁺ accumulates here during electron transport
• Inner membrane: highly folded into cristae; contains electron transport chain (ETC) complexes and ATP synthase; impermeable to ions
• Matrix: contains Krebs cycle enzymes, mtDNA, mitochondrial ribosomes

The electron transport chain complexes in the inner membrane pump H⁺ into the intermembrane space as electrons pass through them; ATP synthase uses the resulting H⁺ gradient to synthesize ATP. Note: when the H⁺ gradient cannot be relieved by ATP synthase (e.g. if ATP synthase is blocked), electron flow through the chain and O₂ consumption also slow, because the chain works against the built-up gradient.

stem: Which property of water is most directly responsible for the needle remaining on the surface before soap was added?
stimulus: A student placed a steel needle carefully on the surface of water in a bowl. The needle floated despite being denser than water. When a drop of dish soap was added near the needle, it immediately sank. A classmate observed that water strider insects exploit the same property to walk across pond surfaces.

choices.text: Adhesion between water molecules and the needle's metal surface
Cohesion between water molecules generating surface tension
Water's high specific heat capacity, which slows the needle's movement into the surface
The evaporation of water from the surface creating an upward pressure on the needle

stem: Which statement best explains why a transport protein can distinguish between these two sugars?
stimulus: Glucose and fructose are monosaccharides with the same molecular formula, C6H12O6, but their atoms are arranged differently, so the two molecules have different three-dimensional shapes. A transport protein in the plasma membrane of intestinal cells moves fructose across the membrane much more efficiently than it moves glucose.

choices.text: They have different numbers of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen atoms, so the protein recognizes the sugar with more atoms.
They differ in the number of hydroxyl groups attached to the sugar backbone, and the protein recognizes the extra groups.
They have the same atoms arranged differently, which gives them different three-dimensional shapes that fit the transport protein differently.
Fructose is a polysaccharide, so it must be moved by a different kind of transport protein than glucose.

stem: Which property of water explains the large energy transfer associated with evaporation, and which property explains why liquid water beads and rolls along hydrophobic troughs rather than spreading flat?
stimulus: Namib Desert beetles collect water by tilting toward coastal fog at dawn. Droplets condense on hydrophilic bumps on their back surfaces and roll toward their mouths along hydrophobic troughs. Researchers noted that beetles must collect water before peak daytime heat causes significant evaporative loss from their body surface. A separate study found that transferring the same mass of water from liquid to vapor requires substantially more energy than melting the same mass of ice.

choices.text: High specific heat explains both phenomena: it slows temperature change and causes water to resist spreading on surfaces.
Adhesion explains both: water clings to hydrophilic bumps and rolls along hydrophobic troughs because it adheres strongly to both surfaces.
Polarity alone explains both: polar water requires no energy to vaporize and is repelled by every nonpolar surface.
High heat of vaporization means each gram that evaporates absorbs substantial energy; cohesion keeps water molecules attracted to one another so they bead on hydrophobic surfaces.

stem: Which best explains the molecular basis for HbS polymerization under low-oxygen conditions?
stimulus: Sickle cell disease results from a single amino acid substitution in β-globin: glutamic acid (polar, negatively charged at pH 7.4) at position 6 is replaced by valine (nonpolar, hydrophobic). Under low-oxygen conditions, sickle hemoglobin (HbS) polymerizes into rigid fibers that deform red blood cells. Normal hemoglobin (HbA) does not polymerize under the same conditions.

choices.text: Valine's smaller side chain leaves a gap that destabilizes β-globin's alpha-helix, unfolding HbS into fibers
The hydrophobic valine at position 6 inserts into the complementary hydrophobic pocket exposed on adjacent deoxygenated HbS molecules, driving chain polymerization through hydrophobic interactions
Valine disrupts the disulfide bonds that normally maintain hemoglobin's quaternary structure, causing uncontrolled aggregation
The loss of glutamic acid's negative charge at position 6 directly prevents HbS from binding oxygen, causing polymerization as an indirect consequence

stem: Which best explains why celery in distilled water becomes rigid rather than lysing, unlike animal cells in hypotonic solution?
stimulus: A student places strips of celery into three solutions for 30 minutes: (1) distilled water, (2) dilute salt solution, and (3) concentrated salt solution. After 30 minutes, the strip in distilled water is rigid and crisp; the strip in dilute salt solution is slightly flexible; the strip in concentrated salt solution is limp and wilted. The student notes that unlike red blood cells placed in distilled water, the celery does not burst.

choices.text: The cellulose cell wall resists expansion after water enters, so rising turgor pressure limits further swelling and prevents lysis.
The plant plasma membrane becomes impermeable to water in distilled water, so the cell wall remains rigid because no osmosis occurs.
Water enters until the cytoplasm becomes isotonic with the surrounding water, at which point net movement stops and the cell stays intact.
Plant cells avoid lysis because their cytoplasm is always isotonic to distilled water, while animal cells are hypertonic to distilled water.

stem: Which best explains why the Na⁺/K⁺ pump must consume ATP rather than operating spontaneously like ion leak channels?
stimulus: The Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase pump in neurons transports 3 Na⁺ out of the cell and 2 K⁺ into the cell per ATP hydrolyzed. In a resting neuron, Na⁺ concentration is approximately 145 mM outside and 12 mM inside; K⁺ is approximately 4 mM outside and 140 mM inside. When neurons are treated with ouabain (a pump inhibitor) and deprived of ATP, these concentration gradients dissipate over 30 minutes as both ions diffuse down their gradients via leak channels.

choices.text: The pump moves Na⁺ and K⁺ in the same direction, requiring energy to overcome electrostatic repulsion between co-transported ions
The pump moves both ions at equal concentrations on both sides of the membrane, and ATP provides the energy to maintain equal distribution
The pump requires ATP because Na⁺ and K⁺ ions are too hydrated to pass through membrane proteins without chemical assistance to strip their water shells

The pump moves Na⁺ out against its inward electrochemical gradient and K⁺ in against its outward concentration gradient — both movements are thermodynamically unfavorable and require free energy input from ATP hydrolysis

stem: Which prediction about individuals with familial hypercholesterolemia is best supported by the described process?
stimulus: Liver cells take up LDL cholesterol by endocytosis. LDL particles bind to LDL receptors, which are proteins in the plasma membrane. The membrane then folds inward and engulfs the bound LDL in a vesicle that carries it into the cell. In familial hypercholesterolemia (FH), mutations eliminate functional LDL receptors from the cell surface.

choices.text: Their liver cells will compensate by taking in large amounts of LDL through nonspecific endocytosis that does not need receptors.
LDL particles will accumulate in the bloodstream because liver cells cannot specifically recognize and take them in without functional receptors.
Their liver cells will take in LDL normally, because endocytosis does not depend on any proteins in the plasma membrane.
Their liver cells will collect LDL inside vesicles, because the vesicles cannot fuse with the plasma membrane to release it.

stem: Which set of solution osmolarities is most consistent with the observed outcomes for Solutions X, Y, and Z respectively?
stimulus: Red blood cells (which lack a cell wall) were placed in three unlabeled solutions for 5 minutes and photographed. In Solution X, cells appeared as normal biconcave discs. In Solution Y, cells swelled to a spherical shape and approximately 30% lysed. In Solution Z, cells developed irregular spiked protrusions (crenation) and shrank. Normal red blood cell cytoplasm has an osmolarity of approximately 300 mOsm/L.

choices.text: X = 500 mOsm/L; Y = 300 mOsm/L; Z = 100 mOsm/L
X = 300 mOsm/L; Y = 100 mOsm/L; Z = 500 mOsm/L
X = 300 mOsm/L; Y = 500 mOsm/L; Z = 100 mOsm/L
X = 100 mOsm/L; Y = 300 mOsm/L; Z = 500 mOsm/L

stem: Which outcome for amylase in the treated cells is most likely?
stimulus: Pancreatic cells secrete the digestive enzyme amylase. Amylase is made by ribosomes on the rough ER. It is then modified and packaged in the Golgi complex, and transport vesicles carry it to the plasma membrane to be secreted. A researcher treats the cells with a drug that blocks the formation of the transport vesicles that carry material from the rough ER to the Golgi complex.

choices.text: Amylase is no longer made at all, because ribosomes on the rough ER cannot make proteins unless vesicles leave the ER.
Amylase is made by ribosomes in the Golgi complex instead, and it is then secreted normally.
Amylase is still made on the rough ER, but it builds up there, and little reaches the Golgi complex or is secreted.
Amylase is secreted faster than normal, because it no longer has to pass through the Golgi complex first.

stem: Which single piece of evidence most specifically supports the claim that a prokaryote was engulfed by a host cell, rather than simply showing a prokaryote-like ancestry?
stimulus: Evidence supporting the endosymbiotic origin of mitochondria includes: (1) mitochondria have a double membrane, with an inner membrane that resembles the plasma membrane of a prokaryote and an outer membrane that resembles the endomembrane of the eukaryotic cell; (2) mitochondria have their own circular DNA, like the chromosome of a prokaryote; (3) mitochondria make some of their own proteins on their own ribosomes; (4) new mitochondria arise from existing mitochondria without the cell having to divide.

choices.text: The double membrane, with an outer layer like host endomembrane and an inner layer like a prokaryotic plasma membrane, matches a prokaryote surrounded by a host membrane.
Having its own circular DNA shows that mitochondria can still survive on their own outside the host cell, as a free-living prokaryote would.
Making new mitochondria without any cell division shows that mitochondria were once free-living prokaryotes that lived on their own.
Having their own ribosomes for making proteins shows that mitochondria are currently prokaryotes that live inside eukaryotic cells.

stem: Which characterization of Protein M is best supported by these results?
stimulus: Researchers study two proteins from red blood cells. Protein M is found with the membranes of broken cells and cannot be separated from the phospholipids unless the bilayer is dissolved. The amino acids on the surface of Protein M have mostly nonpolar R groups. Protein C is found dissolved in the cytoplasm. The amino acids on the surface of Protein C have mostly polar R groups.

choices.text: A protein dissolved in the cytoplasm, with nonpolar R groups on its surface that interact with the surrounding water.
A protein attached only to the outside of the membrane, with its nonpolar R groups facing the watery environment.
A protein embedded in the membrane, with polar R groups on the surface that touches the phospholipid tails.
A protein embedded in the bilayer, with nonpolar R groups on the surface that touches the hydrophobic tails of the phospholipids.

stem: Which conclusion integrating membrane biochemistry and evolutionary ecology is best supported by the data?
stimulus:
Researchers compared plasma membrane phospholipid composition in desert lizards (body temperature 42°C) and deep-sea Antarctic fish (body temperature −1°C):

Species           | % Saturated FA | % Monounsaturated FA | % Polyunsaturated FA
Desert lizard     |      61        |         30           |         9
Antarctic fish    |      17        |         43           |         40

Both species maintain functional (fluid) membranes at their respective environmental temperatures. Desert lizard membranes solidify when cooled to −1°C; Antarctic fish membranes become excessively fluid when warmed to 42°C.

choices.text: Desert lizards evolved high saturated fat content as an energy reserve because hot environments provide insufficient caloric food sources

Natural selection has independently favored membrane compositions that maintain optimal fluidity at each species' functional temperature: unsaturated fatty acids (which have kinked tails that resist tight packing) are enriched in cold-adapted species to prevent membrane crystallization, while saturated fatty acids predominate in heat-adapted species to prevent excessive membrane fluidity
Antarctic fish have more polyunsaturated fatty acids because their diet of krill is rich in omega-3 fatty acids, which are directly incorporated unchanged into membranes
Desert lizards produce saturated fatty acids because saturated fats are metabolically less expensive to synthesize, providing a fitness advantage in resource-limited hot environments

stem: Which best explains why apoptosis — rather than necrosis — is essential for sculpting the spaces between developing digits?
stimulus: During human hand development, interdigital cells undergo programmed cell death (apoptosis). Caspase enzymes are activated by cytochrome c release from mitochondria (intrinsic pathway) and by death-ligand binding to surface receptors (extrinsic pathway). Active caspases systematically dismantle the cell: cleaving cytoskeletal proteins, fragmenting DNA, and producing membrane-bound apoptotic bodies that are phagocytosed by neighboring cells without rupturing. In necrosis, cellular contents spill into surrounding tissue, triggering inflammation. Mice lacking the pro-apoptotic genes Bax and Bak retain webbing between their digits.

choices.text: Necrosis would clear the interdigital cells more efficiently than apoptosis because it does not require ATP-dependent caspase activation
Apoptosis eliminates interdigital cells in an orderly, contained manner that prevents inflammation and preserves the integrity of adjacent digit tissue, allowing precise sculpting of the hand
Apoptosis is faster than necrosis, ensuring interdigital cells are eliminated within the narrow developmental window before digit formation is complete
The Bax/Bak knockout result shows that the extrinsic (death-receptor) pathway alone is sufficient to trigger interdigital apoptosis, since Bax and Bak are intrinsic-pathway genes

stem: Which correctly describes the directionality and template strand usage in transcription and translation?
stimulus: The central dogma describes information flow: DNA → RNA → Protein. During transcription, RNA polymerase moves along the DNA template strand and synthesizes a complementary RNA strand. During translation, the ribosome reads mRNA codons and assembles a polypeptide chain. Both processes follow strict directionality rules based on the chemistry of nucleotide and amino acid addition.

choices.text: Transcription proceeds 3'→5' along the template strand, synthesizing RNA 5'→3'; translation reads mRNA 3'→5', adding amino acids to the N-terminus
Transcription reads the template strand 3'→5' and synthesizes RNA 5'→3'; translation reads mRNA codons 5'→3' and adds each new amino acid to the C-terminus of the growing polypeptide
Transcription reads the coding (non-template) strand 5'→3' to synthesize RNA; translation reads mRNA 5'→3' adding amino acids to the N-terminus
Both transcription and translation proceed 5'→3' along their respective templates, and new monomers are always added to the 5' end of the growing chain

stem: During a sunny afternoon, a pond absorbs substantial heat, but its water temperature rises only slightly. This helps maintain a stable environment for aquatic organisms. Which explanation best accounts for the small temperature change?

choices.text: Heat breaks the covalent bonds within water molecules, giving water a high specific heat capacity.
Water is nonpolar, so its molecules lack attractions to one another and absorb heat with little temperature change.
Water has a low specific heat capacity, so absorbing substantial heat produces only a small temperature increase.
Water's polarity allows hydrogen bonds to form between molecules, and disrupting these interactions absorbs energy, giving water a high specific heat capacity.

stem: A researcher models an organism’s temperature regulation using water and a hypothetical replacement liquid. The replacement molecules are less polar and form weaker hydrogen bonds than water molecules. In one trial, equal masses absorb equal amounts of thermal energy without evaporating. In a second trial, equal masses evaporate, drawing all required energy from the model organism. Considering the effects of weaker hydrogen bonding, which prediction about the replacement liquid is best supported?

choices.text: It undergoes a smaller temperature increase in the first trial and removes less energy from the organism in the second trial.
It undergoes a larger temperature increase in the first trial and removes less energy from the organism in the second trial.
It undergoes a larger temperature increase in the first trial and removes more energy from the organism in the second trial.

stem: Growing cells use phospholipids to build membranes and nucleic acids to store and transmit genetic information. The cells have enough of every required element except phosphorus. Which statement best explains how this shortage limits the production of these molecules?

choices.text: Production of both phospholipids and nucleic acids is limited because both contain phosphorus.
Only nucleic acid production is limited because phospholipids do not contain phosphorus.
Only phospholipid production is limited because nucleic acids require nitrogen instead of phosphorus.
Neither type of molecule is affected because biological molecules require only carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen.

stem: A researcher asks whether phosphorus availability limits cells’ production of DNA, which stores hereditary information. Cells can be grown in media with controlled supplies of each element. All groups start with equal numbers of identical cells and are maintained at the same temperature for the same time. Which experimental design best tests the researcher’s question?

choices.text: Compare DNA production in nitrogen-free and nitrogen-containing media, keeping all other elements equally available in adequate amounts.
Compare DNA production in media lacking both phosphorus and nitrogen with media containing both, keeping all other elements equally available in adequate amounts.
Compare DNA production in phosphorus-free and phosphorus-containing media, keeping all other elements equally available in adequate amounts.
Compare phosphorus-free and phosphorus-containing media, keeping all other elements equally available in adequate amounts, and measure only phosphorus remaining in each medium.

stem: A growing cell uses nucleic acids to store and transmit genetic information and phospholipids to build membranes. Its environment supplies insufficient nitrogen and phosphorus but adequate carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, and sulfur. A researcher restores nitrogen availability to normal without changing phosphorus availability. Assuming the cell has no alternative phosphorus source, which prediction best explains the effect on production of nucleic acids and phospholipids?

choices.text: Nucleic acid production returns to normal, but phospholipid production remains limited because only phospholipids require phosphorus.
Phospholipid production returns to normal, but nucleic acid production remains limited because lipids require only carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen.
Production of both nucleic acids and phospholipids returns to normal because the added nitrogen can replace phosphorus in these molecules.
Production of both nucleic acids and phospholipids remains limited because both require phosphorus.

stem: A cell breaks a long polymer into shorter chains by cleaving covalent bonds between its subunits. Which statement explains the chemical reaction responsible for this change?

choices.text: Hydrolysis releases water as covalent bonds between subunits break.
Hydrolysis consumes water to break covalent bonds between subunits.
Hydrolysis consumes water to form covalent bonds between subunits.
Dehydration synthesis releases water as covalent bonds form between subunits.

stem:
A researcher tracks polymers and free monomers in a reaction mixture. Each polymer contains six monomers joined by covalent bonds.

Time (minutes) | Number of polymers | Number of free monomers
0 | 10 | 0
5 | 5 | 30
10 | 0 | 60

Which statement best describes the trend in the data and the reaction responsible?

choices.text: Polymers decrease as free monomers increase; dehydration synthesis releases water to break covalent bonds.
Polymers decrease as free monomers increase; hydrolysis releases water when it breaks covalent bonds.
Polymers increase as free monomers decrease; dehydration synthesis releases water to form covalent bonds.
Polymers decrease as free monomers increase; hydrolysis consumes water to break covalent bonds.

stem: A cell joins eight separate monomers into one linear polymer by dehydration synthesis. A treatment then causes hydrolysis of exactly three different bonds connecting monomers in that polymer, with no further joining. Considering only these reactions, what final number of separate molecules and net change in water molecules are predicted relative to the start?

choices.text: Four separate molecules derived from the polymer; ten water molecules released overall.
Four separate molecules derived from the polymer; four water molecules released overall.
Four separate molecules derived from the polymer; four water molecules consumed overall.
Three separate molecules derived from the polymer; four water molecules released overall.

stem: Researchers study a mutant plant that cannot synthesize cellulose. Its cells form weak cell walls, and the plant cannot hold its stem upright. Which statement best explains this observation?

choices.text: Cellulose is a polysaccharide of glucose monomers covalently linked into long linear chains that give plant cell walls structural support.
Cellulose is the main energy-storage polysaccharide in plants, so without it the cells lack the fuel needed to grow upright.
Cellulose is a monosaccharide that plant cells break down for quick energy, so the cells cannot fuel cell wall construction.
Cellulose is a protein whose folded amino acid chains form fibers, so without it the wall loses its folded protein framework.

stem: A researcher wants to test whether cellulose contributes to structural support in plant tissue. A treatment selectively removes cellulose without removing starch or other polysaccharides. Which experimental design best tests this question?

choices.text: Randomly assign equal-sized strips from the same plant tissue to the treatment or an otherwise identical control solution, then compare the amount of starch stored in the strips.
Apply the treatment to thin strips and an otherwise identical control solution to thick strips from the same plant tissue, then compare the force required to tear them.
Apply the treatment to all equal-sized strips from the same plant tissue, then measure the force required to tear each strip and calculate the average.

Randomly assign equal-sized strips from the same plant tissue to the treatment or an otherwise identical solution without the cellulose-removing agent, then compare the force required to tear the strips.

stem: A plant seedling carries a mutation that inactivates the enzyme that joins glucose monomers into cellulose. Photosynthesis still produces glucose at normal rates, and the enzyme that joins glucose into starch works normally. Which prediction about the mutant seedling is best supported?

choices.text: It will be unable to store energy, because cellulose is the main energy-storage polysaccharide in plants.
Its cell walls will stay strong, because starch is also a glucose polymer and will take over the structural role of cellulose.
Its cell walls will be weak, so the seedling will have poor structural support, while its ability to store energy as starch will be largely unaffected.
It will lack glucose for cellular energy, because the mutation prevents glucose from being produced.

stem: Two fats have fatty acid chains of similar lengths. Fat X contains more unsaturated fatty acids and is liquid at room temperature, while fat Y contains more saturated fatty acids and is solid. Which explanation best accounts for this difference?

choices.text: Unsaturated fatty acids in fat X contain only single carbon–carbon bonds, which introduce kinks.
Double bonds straighten fat X’s fatty acid chains, allowing tighter packing.
Double bonds make fat X’s fatty acid chains hydrophilic, causing it to be liquid.
Double bonds introduce kinks in fat X’s fatty acid chains, preventing tight packing.

stem:
A student compares three fat samples whose fatty acid chains have the same length but different numbers of carbon–carbon double bonds. The student records the following results.

Sample | Double bonds per fatty acid chain | Melting temperature (°C)
X | 0 | 60
Y | 1 | 15
Z | 2 | −5

Which statement best describes the relationship in the data and explains it using fatty acid structure?

choices.text: More double bonds are associated with higher melting temperatures because unsaturated fatty acid chains are straighter and pack more closely.
More double bonds are associated with lower melting temperatures because kinks in unsaturated fatty acid chains interfere with close packing.
More double bonds are associated with lower melting temperatures because double bonds make the fats hydrophilic.
More double bonds are associated with lower melting temperatures because adding double bonds makes the fatty acid chains more saturated.

stem: A change in a mammal’s diet increases the proportion of unsaturated fatty acids in its stored fats. The total mass of stored fat and the lengths of the fatty acid chains remain unchanged. At the same temperature, which prediction best connects the structural change to the properties and function of the stored fats?

choices.text: The stored fats will tend to be less liquid while continuing to serve as a long-term energy reserve.
The stored fats will tend to be more liquid and become water-soluble, preventing them from serving as an energy reserve.
The stored fats will tend to be more liquid and form phospholipid bilayers instead of serving as an energy reserve.
The stored fats will tend to be more liquid while continuing to serve as a long-term energy reserve.

stem: Two DNA segments have the same length and the same total number of each base, but their bases occur in different orders. Which statement best explains how the biological information stored in these segments compares?

choices.text: They must store the same information because they contain the same number of nucleotides.
They can store different information because information is encoded in the order of their nucleotides.
They must store the same information because they contain the same total number of each base.
They must store the same information because both have repeating sugar-phosphate backbones.

stem: A researcher mixes a single-stranded DNA molecule with a second single strand that is complementary and antiparallel to it, then measures the percentage of molecules that form double strands. The researcher wants to show that pairing depends on complementary base sequence, not merely on the presence of a second DNA strand with the same bases. Which additional treatment is the most appropriate control?

The same complementary DNA strand added at twice the concentration
The original single strand alone, with no second strand added
A DNA strand of the same length and the same number of each base as the complementary strand, but in an order that is not complementary

stem: One strand of a double-stranded DNA segment has the sequence 5′-ACGTTA-3′. A change replaces the second nucleotide, C, with A; all other nucleotides remain unchanged. stem: A protein consists of a single polypeptide chain. In a second version of the protein, one amino acid with a hydrophobic R group is replaced by an amino acid with a charged R group. The second version folds differently and functions less effectively. Which explanation best connects the amino acid replacement to these observations?

choices.text: The two versions have identical primary structures because they contain the same number of amino acids, so sequence cannot explain the functional difference.
Only peptide bonds determine the protein’s folded shape, so changing an R group cannot explain the functional difference.
The replacement changes quaternary structure because quaternary structure describes how a single polypeptide folds into its functional shape.
The replacement changes R-group interactions, which can alter the protein’s three-dimensional shape and function.

stem:
Researchers compare two versions of a protein that binds a target molecule. Each version consists of one intact polypeptide containing 100 amino acids. The versions differ only in the amino acid at position 40. Measurements are made under identical conditions.

Protein version | R group at position 40 | Folded shape | Protein molecules bound to target (%)
Original | Hydrophobic | Reference shape | 90
Modified | Charged | Different from reference | 20

Which statement best describes the relationship in the data and connects it to protein structure and function?

choices.text: The versions have identical primary structures because they contain the same number of amino acids, so the binding difference cannot reflect a sequence change.
The modified protein binds fewer target molecules because replacing the R group breaks peptide bonds and shortens the polypeptide.
The modified protein’s different folded shape represents a change in quaternary structure that explains its lower target binding.
The modified protein has a different folded shape and lower target binding, consistent with changed R-group interactions affecting protein function.

stem: A protein consists of a single polypeptide and binds a small molecule in a pocket formed by its folded structure. A hydrophobic amino acid buried near the pocket is replaced with an amino acid that has a charged R group. The chain length and peptide-bond connections remain unchanged. Which prediction best connects this replacement to protein function?

choices.text: Intact peptide-bond connections preserve the primary structure, so the pocket’s shape and binding ability must remain unchanged.
The replacement changes secondary structure because secondary structure is defined by R-group interactions, reducing binding to the small molecule.
Altered R-group interactions may change tertiary structure and the pocket’s shape, reducing binding to the small molecule.
The replacement disrupts quaternary structure by separating the protein’s polypeptide subunits, reducing binding to the small molecule.

stem: In separate trials under identical conditions, enzyme E increases the rate at which substrate X is converted to product but does not increase the conversion rate of substrate Y. The substrates have similar sizes but different shapes and charge distributions. Which explanation best accounts for these results?

choices.text: E’s active site is compatible with X but not Y, allowing E to supply the energy needed for X’s reaction.
E’s active site is compatible with X but not Y, allowing E to raise the activation energy for X’s reaction.
E’s active site fits both substrates because they have similar sizes, so E should accelerate both reactions.
E’s active site is compatible with X but not Y, allowing E to lower the activation energy for X’s reaction.

stem:
A researcher tests the same enzyme with two different substrates in separate reaction mixtures. Within each substrate test, conditions are identical except for the presence or absence of the enzyme. The measured initial reaction rates are:

Substrate | Without enzyme | With enzyme
X | 2 units/min | 20 units/min
Y | 2 units/min | 2 units/min

Which explanation best connects these results to how enzymes function?

choices.text: Substrate X fits the enzyme’s active site, allowing the enzyme to lower the activation energy for its reaction.
The enzyme supplies energy to substrate X, enabling its reaction to occur faster.
Substrate X fits the enzyme’s active site, allowing the enzyme to raise the activation energy for its reaction.
The enzyme lowers activation energy for both reactions because an enzyme can catalyze reactions involving any substrate.

stem:
A researcher measures an enzyme’s initial reaction rate at different pH values. Temperature and initial enzyme and substrate concentrations are identical in every assay. One enzyme sample is first exposed to pH 4, then returned to pH 7 before fresh substrate is added.

Enzyme treatment | Initial reaction rate (relative units)
pH 4 | 2
pH 7 | 12
pH 10 | 2
pH 4, then returned to pH 7 | 12

Which statement best describes the results and explains the effect of pH on enzyme function?

choices.text: Activity is highest at pH 7 among the tested values, and recovery after exposure to pH 4 is consistent with a reversible change in enzyme shape.
Activity increases continuously as pH increases because higher pH always improves the fit between enzyme and substrate.
Exposure to pH 4 permanently denatures the enzyme, so its activity cannot recover when pH 7 is restored.
Exposure to pH 4 breaks the enzyme’s peptide bonds, and restoring pH 7 rebuilds its amino-acid chain.

stem: An enzyme catalyzes a reaction most rapidly at 37°C. Researchers raise the temperature to 70°C while keeping pH and enzyme and substrate concentrations constant. Structural analysis shows that heating disrupts hydrogen bonds and changes the active site's shape. Which prediction best explains how this temperature change will affect the reaction rate?

choices.text: The rate will increase because higher temperature always increases collisions between enzyme and substrate.
The rate will decrease because the altered active site binds substrate less effectively.
The rate will remain unchanged because disrupting hydrogen bonds does not change the amino acid sequence.
The rate will remain unchanged because catalysts are not consumed during the reactions they catalyze.

stem: A cell moves a solute from a lower concentration outside the cell to a higher concentration inside. A membrane transport protein couples this movement to ATP hydrolysis. Which statement best explains how ATP supports this process?

choices.text: Energy released by ATP hydrolysis drives solute movement against its concentration gradient.
ATP hydrolysis creates new energy that drives solute movement against its concentration gradient.
Solute movement against its concentration gradient releases energy that drives ATP synthesis.
ATP supplies energy for solute movement while remaining chemically unchanged.

stem: A cell synthesizes a polymer from monomers through an energy-requiring reaction coupled to ATP hydrolysis. A treatment disrupts this coupling without affecting the enzymes involved. ATP hydrolysis continues at the same rate, ATP and monomer concentrations remain constant, and no alternative energy-releasing reaction is coupled to polymer synthesis. Which prediction and explanation best describe the immediate effect of the treatment?

choices.text: Polymer synthesis remains unchanged because ATP hydrolysis anywhere in the cell supplies the energy needed for synthesis.
Polymer synthesis decreases because energy released by ATP hydrolysis is no longer coupled to the energy-requiring synthesis reaction.
Polymer synthesis remains unchanged because its enzymes eliminate the need for energy input.
Polymer synthesis decreases because ATP hydrolysis has a net energy cost that takes energy away from synthesis.

stem:
Researchers measure photosynthesis in intact chloroplasts at three light intensities while keeping CO₂ availability and temperature constant. Rates are measured after they stabilize and are reported in relative units per minute.

Light intensity | Oxygen production rate | Carbohydrate production rate
Low | 2 | 1
Medium | 4 | 2
High | 6 | 3

Which statement accurately describes the pattern and connects it to the roles of the two stages of photosynthesis?

choices.text: Both production rates increase with light intensity; the light reactions directly produce carbohydrates in the thylakoids.
Both production rates increase with light intensity; the light reactions supply ATP and NADPH for carbohydrate production in the stroma.
Both production rates increase with light intensity; the oxygen is released when CO₂ is split during the Calvin cycle.
Both production rates increase with light intensity; the Calvin cycle supplies ATP and NADPH to power the light reactions.

stem: Which statement best explains how the light reactions and the Calvin cycle work together to produce carbohydrates in a chloroplast?

choices.text: The light reactions in the stroma produce ATP and NADPH that support carbohydrate production by the Calvin cycle in the thylakoid membranes.
The Calvin cycle in the stroma produces ATP and NADPH that supply energy for the light reactions in the thylakoid membranes.
The light reactions in the thylakoid membranes produce ATP and NADPH that support carbohydrate production by the Calvin cycle in the stroma.
Light absorbed in the stroma directly powers carbohydrate production by the Calvin cycle, making ATP and NADPH from the light reactions unnecessary.

stem:
A researcher supplies equal amounts of respiratory substrates to three samples of intact, isolated mitochondria. Temperature, pH, and the number of mitochondria are held constant. The researcher measures ATP production at different oxygen concentrations.

Oxygen concentration (µmol/L) | ATP production rate (nmol/min)
0 | 0
5 | 12
10 | 24

Which statement best describes the relationship in the data and explains oxygen’s role?

choices.text: Over the tested range, ATP production increases with oxygen concentration because oxygen directly joins ADP and phosphate to form ATP.
Over the tested range, ATP production increases with oxygen concentration because oxygen donates electrons to the electron transport chain.
Over the tested range, ATP production increases with oxygen concentration because oxygen accepts electrons at the end of the electron transport chain.
Over the tested range, ATP production increases with oxygen concentration because oxygen is required for ATP production during glycolysis.

stem: Aerobic eukaryotic cells are supplied with glucose and oxygen. A researcher adds a substance that allows H⁺ to cross the inner mitochondrial membrane without passing through ATP synthase. The substance does not directly affect glycolysis or the electron transport chain. Which prediction best explains the short-term effect on cellular ATP production?

choices.text: ATP production by oxidative phosphorylation increases because faster proton movement across the membrane drives more ATP synthesis.
ATP production by oxidative phosphorylation remains unchanged because oxygen directly supplies the energy for ATP synthesis.
All cellular ATP production stops because glycolysis also requires the mitochondrial proton gradient.
ATP production by oxidative phosphorylation decreases, but glycolysis can still produce ATP.

stem:
A cell is modeled as a cube with its entire surface available for nutrient uptake.

Initial side length: 2 μm
Final side length: 4 μm
Surface area = 6s²; volume = s³, where s is side length.

The maximum nutrient uptake rate per unit surface area and the nutrient requirement per unit volume remain constant. After growth, how does the cell’s maximum nutrient uptake rate per unit volume change, and what does this imply about its ability to meet nutrient demand?

choices.text: It doubles, increasing the ability to meet nutrient demand.
It decreases to one-half its initial value, reducing the ability to meet nutrient demand.
It increases fourfold, increasing the ability to meet nutrient demand.
It remains unchanged, leaving the ability to meet nutrient demand unchanged.

stem:
Researchers compare a cell with a smooth plasma membrane to a cell whose plasma membrane has many folds. All folded surfaces contact the surrounding solution.

Cell | Membrane surface area (μm²) | Volume (μm³)
Smooth | 600 | 1,000
Folded | 1,200 | 1,000

Both cells have the same maximum nutrient uptake rate per unit membrane area and the same nutrient requirement per unit volume. Which claim about the effect of membrane folding is best supported by these data?

choices.text: Folding leaves maximum nutrient uptake unchanged, because cells with equal volumes have equal capacities to exchange nutrients.
Folding doubles maximum nutrient uptake without increasing nutrient demand, because it increases exchange surface while maintaining cell volume.
Folding reduces maximum nutrient uptake, because a higher surface area-to-volume ratio makes nutrient exchange less efficient.
Folding doubles nutrient demand without changing maximum nutrient uptake, because demand depends on membrane area while uptake depends on volume.

stem: A researcher constructs a membrane consisting only of a phospholipid bilayer, with no proteins. Oxygen (O₂) is a small, nonpolar molecule, and sodium (Na⁺) is a small, charged ion. Which prediction about their ability to cross this membrane is best supported by membrane structure?

choices.text: Both O₂ and Na⁺ cross readily because both particles are small.
Na⁺ crosses readily, but O₂ passage is strongly restricted because the phospholipid heads are hydrophilic.
Neither O₂ nor Na⁺ crosses readily because all substances require membrane proteins to cross.
O₂ crosses readily, but Na⁺ passage is strongly restricted because the bilayer interior is hydrophobic.

stem: A researcher removes the cell walls from one group of plant cells without damaging their plasma membranes. A second group retains its cell walls. Both groups are then placed in conditions that cause water to enter the cells. Which prediction is best supported by the functions of these cell structures?

choices.text: Cells without walls are less likely to rupture because their plasma membranes can expand without restriction.
Cells without walls are more likely to rupture because they lack the walls’ structural support.
Cells without walls lose selective permeability because the wall determines which molecules cross the plasma membrane.
Both groups are equally likely to rupture because plasma membranes provide the same structural support as cell walls.

stem: An uncharged solute initially has a concentration of 10 mmol/L outside a cell and 2 mmol/L inside. A membrane protein allows net movement of the solute into the cell without energy input. Which statement correctly explains this transport?

choices.text: The transport is active because movement through any membrane protein requires energy input.
The transport is active because inward movement takes the solute from lower to higher concentration.
The transport is passive because the solute moves down its concentration gradient without energy input.
The transport is passive, so solute molecules will stop moving once the concentrations become equal.

stem:
A researcher measures membrane events in two otherwise identical cell samples over 10 minutes. One sample has normal cellular energy availability; the other has greatly reduced energy availability.

Average events per cell:
Membrane event | Normal energy | Reduced energy
Membrane folds inward and engulfs large particles | 40 | 4
Vesicle fuses with plasma membrane and releases contents outside | 60 | 6

Which statement correctly describes the results and identifies the transport processes?

choices.text: Reduced energy availability is associated with fewer events of both types; inward engulfment is exocytosis, and release through vesicle fusion is endocytosis.
Only inward engulfment requires energy; release through vesicle fusion is passive because the contents move out of the cell.
Both events are passive transport because any movement of material across the plasma membrane is diffusion.
Reduced energy availability is associated with fewer endocytosis and exocytosis events; both processes require energy.

stem: Lysosomes contain enzymes that break down macromolecules. Many macromolecules in the cytoplasm must remain intact for the cell to function. Which statement best explains how the membrane surrounding a lysosome benefits the cell?

choices.text: It separates digestive reactions from the cytoplasm, reducing interactions between digestive enzymes and functional cellular macromolecules.
It distributes digestive enzymes throughout the cytoplasm, allowing digestion without interfering with other cellular processes.
It prevents all molecular exchange with the cytoplasm, allowing the lysosome to function independently of the cell.
It increases the surface area of the plasma membrane, allowing faster nutrient uptake from the environment.

stem:
A model compares two eukaryotic cells with identical cell volumes and plasma membrane surface areas. Enzymes that carry out a particular set of reactions are attached to an internal membrane.

Cell X: relatively flat internal membrane; total internal membrane area = 20 μm².
Cell Y: extensively folded internal membrane; total internal membrane area = 40 μm².

Each unit of internal membrane area carries the same number of enzyme molecules, and reactants are abundant in both cells. Which statement best explains the functional advantage represented by Cell Y?

choices.text: Both cells support the same number of simultaneous reactions because their cell volumes are identical.
Cell Y exchanges nutrients with its surroundings faster because its internal folds increase plasma membrane surface area.
Cell Y supports fewer simultaneous reactions because folding reduces the internal membrane area available for enzymes.
Cell Y can support more simultaneous reactions because its greater internal membrane area accommodates more enzyme molecules.

stem: Galactose and glucose are monosaccharides that both have the molecular formula C6H12O6, but one hydroxyl group is oriented differently, so the two molecules have different three-dimensional shapes. A permease in the plasma membrane of yeast cells imports galactose far more slowly than it imports glucose. Which statement best explains why the permease can distinguish between the two sugars?

choices.text: The sugars contain different elements, so the permease binds glucose because it carries more atoms of carbon than galactose does.
The sugars contain the same atoms in different arrangements, so their shapes differ and only glucose fits the binding site of the permease well.
Galactose is a lipid with a hydrophobic backbone, so the permease cannot move it through the membrane as quickly as glucose.
The sugars are joined by different types of covalent bonds, so the permease recognizes the sugar that has the stronger bonds.

stem: Two tripeptides are made from the same three amino acids, alanine, glycine, and serine, but in the order Ala-Gly-Ser in one and Ser-Gly-Ala in the other. An antibody binds the first peptide strongly and the second one very weakly. Which statement best explains why the antibody can tell the two peptides apart?

choices.text: The peptides have different total masses because order changes atoms, so the antibody binds the peptide with the greater mass.
The peptides have the same composition but different sequences, so the groups are arranged differently in space and fit the antibody differently.
The peptides contain different amino acids, so the antibody binds the peptide that has the larger number of different R groups.
The peptides use different kinds of covalent linkages between subunits, so the antibody binds the one with peptide bonds.

stem: A mutation in a bacterial enzyme replaces a serine (polar, uncharged) on the protein's surface with leucine (nonpolar, hydrophobic). The mutant enzyme folds normally and remains active, but in water its molecules clump together into large aggregates, whereas the normal enzyme stays dispersed. Which best explains why the mutant molecules aggregate?

choices.text: The leucine side chains form peptide bonds with neighboring enzyme molecules, joining the proteins into one large covalent polymer.
The exposed nonpolar leucine side chains on separate molecules associate with each other to avoid water, linking the molecules through hydrophobic interactions.
The leucine side chains form strong hydrogen bonds with water, which pulls the molecules together into aggregates.
The leucine substitution adds a negative charge, so the neighboring molecules are attracted to each other by ionic bonds.

stem: Two subunits of a dimeric enzyme normally associate at an interface where aspartate 40 (negatively charged) on subunit A sits next to lysine 112 (positively charged) on subunit B. A mutation replaces lysine 112 with glutamate (negatively charged). The mutant subunits fold correctly but no longer form stable dimers. Which best explains the loss of dimer formation?

choices.text: The attraction between opposite charges is lost and the two negatively charged side chains now repel each other at the interface.
The mutation breaks the peptide bond at position 112, so the subunit is cut in two and cannot reach the interface.
Glutamate is nonpolar, so it moves into the core of the subunit and no longer faces the interface where it could bind.
The glutamate side chain forms a disulfide bond with aspartate 40, which locks the surface of subunit B in the wrong shape.

stem: In a small globular enzyme, valine at position 73 is normally buried in the interior of the folded protein, surrounded by other nonpolar side chains. A mutation replaces valine 73 with aspartate, which has a negatively charged side chain. The mutant protein folds poorly and loses most of its activity at body temperature. Which best explains this effect?

choices.text: The negative charge of aspartate forms hydrogen bonds that are stronger than hydrophobic interactions and so improve stability.
Aspartate cannot form peptide bonds, so the polypeptide chain is cut at position 73 and the enzyme is shorter than normal.
A charged side chain placed in the nonpolar interior cannot interact favorably with the surrounding nonpolar groups, destabilizing the folded tertiary structure.
The aspartate substitution changes the primary structure only, and primary structure has no effect on folding of the polypeptide.

stem: A student weighs a potato core, places it in 0.6 M sucrose for one hour, and reweighs it. The core's mass falls from 5.0 g to 4.3 g, a change of -14%, and the tissue feels limp. A core placed in distilled water instead gains mass and feels firm. Which best explains the limp tissue in 0.6 M sucrose?

choices.text: Sucrose entered the cells through the cell wall and replaced the cytoplasm, so the cells lost mass through exchange of sugar.
Water left the cells by osmosis because the sucrose solution was hypertonic, so turgor pressure fell and the tissue became limp.
The cells stopped using osmosis in sucrose, so the tissue lost mass through evaporation rather than through water movement.
Water entered the cells until the cell wall burst, which released fluid into the solution and lowered the mass.

stem: Plant biologists treat leaf cells with enzymes that digest the cellulose cell wall, producing protoplasts. Intact leaf cells placed in distilled water become firm but stay intact, whereas protoplasts placed in distilled water swell and many burst. Which best explains the difference in outcome?

choices.text: Protoplasts lose their plasma membranes during digestion, so distilled water flows freely through them until they rupture.
Intact cells stay whole because their cytoplasm is isotonic to distilled water, whereas the protoplasts become hypotonic to it.
Without a wall, protoplasts have nothing to resist water entering by osmosis, so no turgor pressure limits swelling and the membrane ruptures.
The enzyme treatment makes the cytoplasm of protoplasts hypertonic to the intact cells, so water moves out until they burst.

stem: A gardener waters houseplants with a very salty solution. Within hours the leaves droop, and under a microscope the plasma membranes of the leaf cells have pulled away from the cell walls. Plants watered with fresh water stay upright and firm. Which best explains why the plants watered with salty solution droop?

choices.text: Salt entered the cells and made the cell walls swell, which pushed the plasma membranes away from the cell walls.
The cell walls dissolved in the salty solution, so the cells could no longer hold any water and the leaves drooped.
Water moved out of the cells by osmosis into the salty surroundings, so the cells lost turgor pressure and the tissue wilted.
Water moved into the cells until the walls cracked, so the cells became flaccid and the leaves drooped.

stem: Pancreatic beta cells store insulin in secretory vesicles. When blood glucose rises, the vesicles move to the plasma membrane, fuse with it, and release insulin outside the cell by exocytosis. A toxin prevents secretory vesicles from fusing with the plasma membrane but does not affect insulin synthesis. Which prediction is best supported by the described process?

choices.text: Insulin will be taken up into the cells by endocytosis, which lowers the amount of insulin in the vesicles.
Insulin will build up inside undelivered vesicles, and blood glucose will stay high because little insulin is released from the cells.
Insulin will diffuse through the phospholipid bilayer instead, so blood glucose will fall at the normal rate.
Beta cells will stop making insulin completely, because the toxin blocks translation on ribosomes of the rough ER.

stem: Animal cells without a cell wall, whose cytoplasm has an osmolarity of about 280 mOsm/L, were placed in three unlabeled solutions for 10 minutes. In Solution P, the cells kept their normal shape. In Solution Q, the cells shrank and their surfaces became wrinkled. In Solution R, the cells swelled and about half burst. Which set of osmolarities is most consistent with the outcomes for P, Q, and R respectively?

choices.text: P = 600 mOsm/L; Q = 280 mOsm/L; R = 50 mOsm/L
P = 50 mOsm/L; Q = 280 mOsm/L; R = 600 mOsm/L
P = 280 mOsm/L; Q = 600 mOsm/L; R = 50 mOsm/L
P = 280 mOsm/L; Q = 50 mOsm/L; R = 600 mOsm/L

stem: Cultured animal cells with no cell wall have a cytoplasmic osmolarity of 300 mOsm/L. The cells are placed in three solutions that contain only solutes unable to cross the plasma membrane: Solution A at 150 mOsm/L, Solution B at 300 mOsm/L, and Solution C at 450 mOsm/L. Which set of outcomes is most likely for the cells in A, B, and C respectively?

choices.text: A: cells swell and may lyse; B: no net change in volume; C: cells lose water and shrink
A: cells lose water and shrink; B: no net change in volume; C: cells swell and may lyse
A: no net change in volume; B: cells swell and may lyse; C: cells lose water and shrink
A: cells swell and may lyse; B: cells lose water and shrink; C: no net change in volume

stem: Identical wall-less animal cells were placed in four solutions of non-penetrating solutes for 10 minutes, and the change in cell volume was recorded: Solution 1, +25%; Solution 2, -18%; Solution 3, 0%; Solution 4, -30%. Which ordering of the solutions from lowest to highest osmolarity is most consistent with the data?

choices.text: Solution 4, Solution 2, Solution 3, Solution 1
Solution 1, Solution 2, Solution 3, Solution 4
Solution 3, Solution 2, Solution 1, Solution 4
Solution 1, Solution 3, Solution 2, Solution 4

stem: Plasma cells secrete antibodies. Antibodies are made by ribosomes on the rough ER, transferred to the Golgi complex for modification, and carried in vesicles from the Golgi complex to the plasma membrane for secretion. A drug blocks the fusion of those Golgi vesicles with the plasma membrane. Which outcome for antibody is most likely in the treated cells?

choices.text: Antibody is released from the rough ER directly to the outside of the cell, bypassing the blocked Golgi vesicles.
Antibody is no longer made, because ribosomes on the rough ER stop translating when vesicles cannot fuse with the membrane.
Antibody is still made and enters the Golgi complex and vesicles, but it accumulates inside the cell and little is secreted.
Antibody is made by ribosomes in the vesicles instead, and the cells secrete it by a different route.

stem: Hydrolytic enzymes that digest worn-out cell components are made by ribosomes on the rough ER, then modified and sorted in the Golgi complex into vesicles that become lysosomes. A drug prevents the Golgi complex from packaging these enzymes into vesicles but does not affect enzyme synthesis. Which outcome is most likely in the treated cells?

choices.text: The enzymes are no longer made, because the Golgi complex supplies the ribosomes that carry out their synthesis.
The enzymes are digested by the Golgi complex, so worn-out components are broken down faster than in untreated cells.
The enzymes are made inside the lysosomes instead, so worn-out components are digested at the normal rate.
The enzymes are still made, but they do not reach lysosomes, so worn-out cell components are digested less and accumulate.

stem: A biologist examines four cell types for organelles. Cell W secretes large amounts of a protein hormone. Cell X secretes a steroid hormone, which is a lipid. Cell Y contracts and contains many mitochondria. Cell Z stores fat in a large droplet. Protein destined for secretion is made on the rough ER and then processed by the Golgi complex. Which cell would be expected to have the most extensive rough ER and Golgi complex?

choices.text: Cell X, because lipids such as steroids are made on the rough ER and then secreted in vesicles from the Golgi.
Cell Z, because a large droplet of fat has to be packaged by the Golgi complex before it can be stored.
Cell W, because making and secreting a large amount of protein depends on the rough ER and Golgi complex.
Cell Y, because the many mitochondria in the cell supply the protein that the rough ER and Golgi complex store.

stem: A transmembrane channel protein forms a pore through the plasma membrane that lets ions pass. Researchers analyze the R groups of its amino acids. Which description of the protein's R groups is most consistent with its location and function?

choices.text: Only nonpolar R groups throughout the protein, since the protein is embedded in the hydrophobic interior of the membrane.
Polar R groups on the outer surface that contacts the phospholipid tails, and nonpolar R groups lining the interior of the pore.
Only polar R groups throughout the protein, since the pore carries ions that are dissolved in the water.
Nonpolar R groups on the outer surface that contacts the phospholipid tails, and polar R groups lining the interior of the pore.

stem: A researcher determines the amino acid sequence of Protein T. Seven separate stretches of about 20 amino acids each have only nonpolar R groups, and the regions between the stretches have mostly polar R groups. Protein T can be removed from membranes only by dissolving the lipid bilayer with a detergent. Which description of Protein T is best supported by these results?

choices.text: A protein attached to the outside of the membrane, with its nonpolar stretches facing the watery fluid around it.
A protein dissolved in the cytoplasm, with its nonpolar stretches facing outward toward the surrounding water.
A protein with all of its polar regions buried in the center of the bilayer, among the hydrophobic tails.
A protein that crosses the bilayer several times, with its nonpolar stretches in the membrane interior and its polar regions outside the bilayer.

stem: Red blood cells contain aquaporin-1 (AQP1) channels. When wild-type red blood cells are moved into a hypotonic solution, they swell and lyse in about 20 seconds. Red blood cells from mice lacking AQP1 also swell and lyse in the same solution, but only after about 60 seconds, which is 3 times as long as the wild type. The solutions and internal osmolarities are identical in both groups. Which explanation best accounts for the difference?

choices.text: Without AQP1, water still crosses by diffusing through the phospholipid bilayer, but more slowly, so the cells swell and lyse after a longer time.
AQP1 channels use ATP to push water into the cell, so cells lacking them have less energy to draw in water.
The knockout cells have a lower internal solute concentration, so the osmotic gradient is smaller and swelling is slower.
Without AQP1, water cannot cross the plasma membrane, so the knockout cells swell only because solutes enter them over time.

topic_evidence.title: Structure of Water and Hydrogen Bonding

stem: A runner's working muscles release heat into surrounding tissues. The tissues' high water content helps prevent a rapid temperature increase. Which explanation links water's molecular structure to this temperature stability?

choices.text: Water's uneven charge distribution enables hydrogen bonding between molecules; disrupting these attractions requires energy, resulting in a high specific heat capacity.
Water absorbs heat by breaking the covalent bonds connecting oxygen and hydrogen within its molecules, resulting in a high specific heat capacity.
Water's nonpolar structure prevents attractions between its molecules, allowing tissues to absorb heat without warming rapidly.
Water's low specific heat capacity means that a large heat input produces only a small temperature increase in tissues.

topic_evidence.title: Structure of Water and Hydrogen Bonding

stem: A greenhouse gardener places sealed containers of water beside young tomato plants. As a heater warms the greenhouse, the water absorbs considerable energy but warms slowly, helping buffer temperature changes around the plants. Which explanation connects this effect to water's molecular structure?

choices.text: Water absorbs energy by breaking the covalent bonds joining oxygen and hydrogen within its molecules, resulting in a high specific heat capacity.
Water's equal charge distribution makes it nonpolar, so the absence of attractions between molecules allows substantial heat absorption with little warming.
Water's uneven charge distribution permits hydrogen bonding between molecules; disrupting these attractions requires energy, resulting in a high specific heat capacity.
Water requires little energy per gram for each degree of warming, so its low specific heat capacity buffers temperature changes.

topic_evidence.title: Structure of Water and Hydrogen Bonding

stem: A biology class grows yeast cultures in tubes surrounded by a water bath. As a heater supplies substantial energy, the bath’s temperature increases only slightly, helping keep the yeast’s environment stable. Which explanation connects this effect to water’s molecular structure?

choices.text: Water’s uneven charge distribution enables hydrogen bonding between molecules; disrupting these attractions takes energy, contributing to a high specific heat capacity.
Energy from the heater breaks covalent O–H bonds inside water molecules, contributing to a high specific heat capacity.
Water has no polar regions, so the absence of attractions between its molecules allows substantial energy absorption with little warming.
Water’s low specific heat capacity allows it to absorb substantial energy while undergoing only a small temperature increase.

topic_evidence.title: Structure of Water and Hydrogen Bonding

stem: Equal masses of water and liquid Y start at the same temperature inside a sealed chamber. Each liquid loses the same amount of heat to the chamber during every 2-minute period, and neither liquid freezes or evaporates. Temperature data: Time (min) | Water (°C) | Liquid Y (°C) — 0 | 40.0 | 40.0; 2 | 38.5 | 34.0; 4 | 37.0 | 28.0. Which statement best describes the cooling pattern and explains the molecular basis of water's response?

choices.text: Water's temperature falls less than liquid Y's because hydrogen bonds forming between its polar molecules release energy as it cools.
Water's temperature falls more than liquid Y's, showing that water has a lower specific heat capacity.
Water's temperature falls less than liquid Y's because new covalent bonds form between its oxygen and hydrogen atoms as it cools.
Water's temperature falls less than liquid Y's because its nonpolar molecules cannot form hydrogen bonds.

topic_evidence.title: Structure of Water and Hydrogen Bonding

stem:
A wildlife center compares two liquids for use in a temperature buffer for an animal enclosure. Equal masses of water and liquid R are warmed from 18°C. The table records the heat absorbed to reach each temperature; no heat escapes, and neither liquid changes phase.

Temperature reached (°C) | Heat absorbed by water (kJ) | Heat absorbed by liquid R (kJ)
18 | 0 | 0
21 | 12 | 3
24 | 24 | 6

Which statement best describes the data and explains water’s thermal behavior?

choices.text: Water requires less heat for the same temperature increase, indicating a lower specific heat capacity than liquid R.
Water requires more heat for the same temperature increase because some absorbed energy disrupts hydrogen bonds between its polar molecules.
Water requires more heat for the same temperature increase because absorbed energy breaks covalent bonds within its molecules.
Water requires more heat for the same temperature increase because its electrically neutral molecules are nonpolar and cannot form hydrogen bonds.

topic_evidence.title: Structure of Water and Hydrogen Bonding

stem:
At a desert field station, equal masses of water and liquid Z sit side by side in sealed, identical containers. During the day both containers absorb the same amount of solar heat, and at night both lose the same amount of heat. Neither liquid evaporates or changes phase.

Temperature data:
Time of day | Water (°C) | Liquid Z (°C)
6:00 | 15 | 8
12:00 | 18 | 20
18:00 | 19 | 26
24:00 | 16 | 12

Which statement best describes the pattern in the data and explains the molecular basis of water's response?

choices.text: Water's temperature varies over a narrower range because energy gained or lost goes partly into breaking or forming hydrogen bonds between its polar molecules.
Water's temperature varies over a wider range, showing that water has a lower specific heat capacity than liquid Z.
Water's temperature varies over a narrower range because absorbed heat breaks the covalent bonds between oxygen and hydrogen atoms within each water molecule.
Water's temperature varies over a narrower range because its molecules are nonpolar and therefore do not form hydrogen bonds.

topic_evidence.title: Structure of Water and Hydrogen Bonding

stem: At a bird hatchery, liquid-filled trays help stabilize egg temperatures, while evaporation from separate wet pads removes heat from the eggs. A proposed synthetic fluid has less polar molecules and weaker intermolecular hydrogen bonds than water. Assume these weaker interactions reduce both its specific heat capacity and its heat of vaporization. Compared with water, how much energy would an equal mass of this fluid require to warm by 2°C without evaporating, and what mass would need to evaporate to remove the same amount of heat from the eggs? Assume all energy for evaporation comes from the eggs.

choices.text: Warming would require more energy, and cooling would require a larger mass to evaporate.
Warming would require less energy, and cooling would require a larger mass to evaporate.
Warming would require less energy, and cooling would require a smaller mass to evaporate.
Warming would require more energy, and cooling would require a smaller mass to evaporate.

topic_evidence.title: Structure of Water and Hydrogen Bonding

stem: An astrobiologist models a hypothetical desert animal whose blood and sweat consist of a solvent whose molecules are less polar than water and form weaker hydrogen bonds with one another. Each afternoon, this animal absorbs the same solar energy as a water-based animal of equal body mass. Both animals cool off by evaporating equal masses of sweat, with all the energy for evaporation drawn from the body. Assuming all other factors are equal, which prediction about the solvent-based animal is best supported?

choices.text: Its body temperature rises less during afternoon heating, and each gram of sweat that evaporates removes less heat from its body.
Its body temperature rises more during afternoon heating, and each gram of sweat that evaporates removes more heat from its body.
Its body temperature rises more during afternoon heating, and each gram of sweat that evaporates removes less heat from its body.
Its body temperature rises less during afternoon heating, and each gram of sweat that evaporates removes more heat from its body.

stem: A researcher separates molecules from a sunflower seed into two purified samples: phospholipids used in membranes and nucleic acids that carry genetic information. Which prediction about phosphorus in these samples is supported by their elemental composition?

choices.text: Phosphorus will be present only in the nucleic acid sample because phospholipids lack phosphorus.
Phosphorus will be present only in the phospholipid sample because nucleic acids contain nitrogen instead.
Phosphorus will be absent from both samples because biological molecules contain only carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen.
Phosphorus will be present in both samples because it is a component of both molecule types.

stem: A waste-recycling project is evaluating discarded fish tissue as a potential phosphorus source. The tissue contains membrane-forming phospholipids and nucleic acids that carry genetic information. Based on their elemental composition, which materials could provide phosphorus for recovery?

choices.text: Both materials could provide phosphorus because phosphorus is part of each molecule type.
Nucleic acids alone could provide phosphorus because phospholipids lack this element.
Phospholipids alone could provide phosphorus because nucleic acids contain nitrogen rather than phosphorus.
Neither material could provide phosphorus because both consist only of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen.

stem: A gardener asks why a fertilizer for tomato plants includes phosphorus. Phospholipids form plant cell membranes, and nucleic acids carry hereditary information. Which explanation connects the fertilizer’s phosphorus to the elemental requirements of these molecules?

choices.text: The phosphorus provides a building material for nucleic acids alone because phospholipids lack this element.
The phosphorus provides a building material required for both phospholipids and nucleic acids.
The phosphorus provides a building material for phospholipids alone because nucleic acids use nitrogen instead.
The phosphorus provides no building material for either molecule because both require only carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen.

stem: A biologist wants to know whether sulfur supply limits how much protein a freshwater alga makes. The alga can be cultured in growth solutions in which the amount of each element is set by the biologist. Every culture begins with the same number of genetically identical algal cells and is kept under the same light and temperature for the same period. Which experimental design best addresses the biologist's question?

choices.text: Grow algae in sulfur-free and sulfur-containing solutions, supply all other elements equally and in adequate amounts, and measure the protein each culture produces.
Grow algae in nitrogen-free and nitrogen-containing solutions, supply all other elements equally and in adequate amounts, and measure the protein each culture produces.
Grow algae in solutions lacking both sulfur and nitrogen and in solutions containing both, supply all other elements equally and in adequate amounts, and measure the protein produced.
Grow algae in sulfur-free and sulfur-containing solutions, supply all other elements equally and in adequate amounts, and measure only how much sulfur is left in each solution.

stem: A microbiologist wonders whether the supply of phosphorus restricts how much phospholipid a soil bacterium makes for building its cell membranes. The bacterium can be grown in liquid cultures in which the quantity of every element is set by the investigator. Each culture is inoculated with the same number of cells from a single clone and incubated under identical temperature, oxygen, and timing conditions. Which procedure is best aligned with the microbiologist's question?

choices.text: Grow cultures with low phosphorus and with ample phosphorus, supply every other element equally and adequately, and measure the amount of phospholipid the cells produce.
Grow cultures with low carbon and with ample carbon, supply every other element equally and adequately, and measure the amount of phospholipid the cells produce.
Grow cultures low in both phosphorus and carbon and cultures ample in both, supply every other element equally and adequately, and measure the amount of phospholipid the cells produce.
Grow cultures with low phosphorus and with ample phosphorus, supply every other element equally and adequately, and measure only how much phosphorus is left in each culture liquid.

stem: A laboratory produces nucleic acids that carry genetic information and phospholipids used in membranes. Two production batches have sufficient carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, and sulfur, but shortages of nitrogen and phosphorus. Batch 1 receives enough nitrogen to eliminate its nitrogen shortage. Batch 2 receives enough nitrogen and phosphorus to eliminate both shortages. Neither batch has another source of either missing element, and no other factor limits production. How should production of the two materials compare between batches?

choices.text: Both materials remain limited in batch 1, whereas both can reach normal production levels in batch 2.
Batch 1 can produce nucleic acids normally but remains limited in phospholipid production; batch 2 can produce both normally.
Batch 1 can produce phospholipids normally but remains limited in nucleic acid production; batch 2 can produce both normally.
Both batches can produce both materials normally because the extra nitrogen in batch 1 can substitute for its missing phosphorus.

stem: A nursery grows duckweed, a small aquatic plant, in nutrient solutions. Duckweed uses nucleic acids for genetic information and phospholipids for membranes. One group initially receives too little nitrogen and phosphorus, while all other required elements are sufficient. A first fertilizer treatment eliminates the nitrogen shortage but supplies no phosphorus. A second treatment then restores phosphorus to a sufficient level. Assuming these shortages are the only limits on production and the plants have no other phosphorus source, how will the second treatment affect nucleic acid and phospholipid production?

choices.text: Only phospholipid production will recover because nucleic acid production already recovered when nitrogen became sufficient.
Only nucleic acid production will recover because phospholipid production was already supported by sufficient carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen.
Neither production rate will change because nitrogen from the first treatment already replaced phosphorus in both materials.
Production of both materials can return to normal because the second treatment supplies an element required by both.

stem: An algae-production facility changes the nutrient mixture supplied to its cultures. The original mixture provided adequate amounts of every required element; the replacement supplies twice as much nitrogen but too little phosphorus, with all other required elements still adequate. The algae make nucleic acids for genetic information and phospholipids for membranes. After stored phosphorus is exhausted, and with no other phosphorus source, how should production of these materials compare with production before the change?

choices.text: Production of both materials decreases because the phosphorus shortage restricts construction of both nucleic acids and phospholipids.
Nucleic acid production stays at its previous rate because nitrogen is sufficient, while phospholipid production decreases because phosphorus is scarce.
Phospholipid production stays at its previous rate because carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen are sufficient, while nucleic acid production decreases.
Production of both materials stays at its previous rate because the extra nitrogen substitutes for the missing phosphorus.

stem: A laboratory sample contains a polymer made of 20 subunits. After a reaction, all 20 subunits are present as separate monomers. Which statement explains the chemical process that separated them?

choices.text: Hydrolysis uses water to cleave the covalent bonds linking the monomers.
Hydrolysis produces water when it cleaves the covalent bonds linking the monomers.
Hydrolysis uses water to create covalent bonds linking the monomers.
Dehydration synthesis produces water when it creates covalent bonds linking the monomers.

stem: A beetle digests a food polymer, producing smaller fragments by separating linked subunits. Which statement explains the chemical reaction that produces these fragments?

choices.text: Hydrolysis produces water while cleaving covalent bonds linking the subunits.
Hydrolysis uses water to create covalent bonds linking the subunits.
Hydrolysis uses water to cleave covalent bonds linking the subunits.
Dehydration synthesis produces water while creating covalent bonds linking the subunits.
